title: The Siege of Vienna
description: September-October 1529. Suleiman the Magnificent's army arrives before Vienna's medieval walls. The player commands the garrison of German Landsknechts and Spanish arquebusiers under Niklas Graf Salm: countermine the Ottoman sappers, repel assaults on the Carinthian Gate, and hold until autumn rains and supply failure force the Ottoman withdrawal.

anachronisms_found: FREDERICK_BARBAROSSA stands in for Niklas Graf Salm: a Hohenstaufen emperor who died in 1190, roughly 340 years before the siege and not a defender of Vienna
SALADIN represents Suleiman the Magnificent: a 12th-century Ayyubid sultan, wrong dynasty, wrong century, wrong theatre entirely

No Janissaries or Hand Cannoneers anywhere despite the text naming janissaries and Spanish arquebusiers; the engine's Turkish Janissary and generic Hand Cannoneer were both available and were avoidably omitted
CAMEL_RIDER x5 in the Ottoman siege lines outside Vienna: the Sipahi cavalry named in the dialogue were horsemen, and camels have no place on the Austrian Danube plain

KNIGHT x4 and MAN_AT_ARMS x4 as the Viennese garrison: mounted knights and mail-clad men-at-arms instead of the Landsknecht pike blocks the text describes (the Teutonic LANDSKNECHT unit exists in the engine and was not used)
TREBUCHET and MANGONEL as the Ottoman siege train in 1529, when the Sultan's force relied on gunpowder artillery and mines; only the defenders were given BOMBARD_CANNON
CROSSBOWMAN and SKIRMISHER as tower garrison rather than gunpowder infantry, contradicting the stated 'arquebusiers to the towers'

issues_found: Player 1's commander is FREDERICK_BARBAROSSA, a 12th-century Hohenstaufen emperor, standing in for Niklas Graf Salm; the defeat trigger literally reads 'Salm Falls' on Barbarossa's death. A renamed generic unit (or the Teutonic/Landsknecht-style infantry) was available, so importing a different named historical figure is avoidable error.

Player 2's Sultan is SALADIN, the Ayyubid sultan of the 1180s, standing in for Suleiman the Magnificent — again a wrong-century named hero where a renamed generic cavalry unit would have been correct.

Both civilizations are left as RANDOM, so architecture set, tech tree and unique units are undefined; the Ottomans could have been assigned Turks (Janissaries, hand cannoneers) and the defenders Teutons/Spanish/Bohemians for a period-plausible skin.

The brief's 'German Landsknechts and Spanish arquebusiers' are represented by 6 crossbowmen and 4 skirmishers plus 2 bombard cannon — the engine's Hand Cannoneer exists and is the obvious stand-in for arquebusiers, so the garrison's defining firearm troops are absent.

Ottoman roster is 5 camel riders and 6 champions rather than janissary-analogue gunpowder infantry; the narration announces 'his janissaries at his back' while the placed units are melee champions and camels, which never featured in the 1529 Vienna army.
Suleiman is made to lead a final charge and be 'struck down' — he neither led an assault in person nor died; the withdrawal came from rain, disease, supply failure and the closing campaign season.
Artillery is inverted: the Ottomans in 1529 had left their heavy siege guns behind in the Danube mud, yet Player 2 gets trebuchet/mangonels while the garrison is handed 2 bombard cannon.
1,756 oak trees dominate a map depicting a walled Danube city and its siege lines; the besieging camp and river frontage are effectively replaced by forest.

Defeat is keyed to the commander's death, but Salm's mortal wound came from a bombardment splinter late in the siege and Vienna still held — the historical failure condition was the city falling, not Salm dying.

SALADIN is placed as Suleiman the Magnificent: a 12th-century Kurdish/Ayyubid sultan standing in for a 16th-century Ottoman, an unrelated era and dynasty. The engine offers renameable generics (Janissary, Champion, Elite Janissary in the Turkish roster) that would have been correct.
FREDERICK_BARBAROSSA stands in for Niklas Graf Salm - a Hohenstaufen emperor of the 1180s substituted for a 1529 Landsknecht commander; a renamed Two-Handed Swordsman or Champion was available.
Both players are set to RANDOM civilization, so the architecture, unit lines and language of the Ottoman besiegers and the Imperial garrison are arbitrary rather than Turkish/Teutonic-Spanish.
No gunpowder infantry anywhere: the brief's Spanish arquebusiers are represented by CROSSBOWMAN and SKIRMISHER although HAND_CANNONEER exists in the engine.

The defenders are given 2 BOMBARD_CANNON and 4 KNIGHT while the Ottomans get only a TREBUCHET and MANGONEL - inverting the actual artillery situation and adding a knightly cavalry arm the Vienna garrison did not field.
CAMEL_RIDER x5 in the Ottoman siege lines is an Egyptian/Levantine flavour unit with no place before Vienna in 1529.

The narration and victory trigger assert that Suleiman personally led the final charge and was killed ('Suleiman's banner falls') - he was never at the breach and withdrew alive to reign another 37 years.
Victory is keyed to killing the sultan, whereas the historical garrison had only to survive until the campaign season closed; the encoded goal is a decapitation raid, not a hold.
The 'Salm Falls' defeat text has him mortally wounded on the ramparts, which conflates his March 1530 death from wounds with an immediate collapse of the garrison.
